Mira Chen: Heads-up — after the kernelselect tweak merged yesterday I'm seeing a regression on multi-GPU cross-node runs. All-reduce time spiked on EFA clusters.
Raj Patel: Can you paste the profiler output / traces?
Mira Chen: Sure — pasted below (condensed):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY
run_id: r2026-03-15-efa
rank 0 allreduce_count: 412   total_allreduce_bytes: 3.3MB   avg_latency_ms: 1.8
rank 1 allreduce_count: 428   total_allreduce_bytes: 3.2MB   avg_latency_ms: 2.1
compute_util: 78%   comm_overlap: 12%
small_allreduces: 320 (<=16KB)
kernel_selected: fused_matmul_v2.fp16 for most matmuls
batch_slicing: enabled (slice_size=64)
kv_prefetch: enabled (prefetch_window=2)
```
Lu Wang: Is this only on EFA or also on NVLink machines?
Mira Chen: Only cross-node EFA so far (2x A100 across racks). NVLink-local jobs look fine. PCIe-only instances show intermediate symptoms.
Raj Patel: @perf-bot run topo-scheduler sweep on r2026-03-15-efa config pls
perf-bot: started job 7890: topo-sweep (targets: EFA, PCIe, NVLink) — will post results when done.
Sofia Morales: Note the kernelselect change: we started preferring `fused_matmul_v2` for fp16 when seq_len >= 256 to save ops. That increases per-op size and shifts token distribution. Might interact poorly with our allreduce batching logic.
Raj Patel: Sounds like the change increases number of small NCCL ops due to different op boundaries?
Mira Chen: Traces confirm fragmentation: lots of small allreduces (~8KB) instead of consolidated larger ones. KV cache prefetch seems to be triggering extra synchronization points.
Lu Wang: Can you try disabling KV prefetch and stopping batch slicing to isolate? Env: `KV_PREFETCH=0 BATCH_SLICING=0`
Mira Chen: Did that earlier today: `KV_PREFETCH=0` reduced allreduce count by ~40%, but per-op latency on PCIe went up ~20%. NVLink still fine. Throughput slightly improved overall but tail latency better on EFA only after additional changes.
Raj Patel: We need comm/compute overlap graphs and NCCL microbenchmarks (allreduce sizes distribution). Also capture kernelselect log for sequence-level decisions.
Mira Chen: Pasted kernelselect snippet:
```
KERNELSELECT LOG
seq_len=512 tokens: prefer fused_matmul_v2 (est_cycles=1.2e6)
seq_len=64  tokens: prefer matmul_v1 (est_cycles=2.8e5)
decision_context: cross_node=true, hw_topology=efa, batch_slice=on
heuristic: cost_per_token + comm_penalty(estimated_allreduce_count)
```
Sofia Morales: Quick mitigation: I'll add a guard in kernelselect: if cross_node && estimated_allreduce_count > 200 -> prefer matmul_v1 or enable chunked-reduce to consolidate. Can test in Canary.
perf-bot: job 7890 finished. Summary: on EFA, allreduce_count reduced 35% when forcing matmul_v1, tail p99 latency improved ~12%, throughput -2%. Full logs: /artifacts/7890/topo-sweep.log
Mira Chen: After Sofia's guard applied in Canary, EFA tail latency improved ~12% and SLOs returned to normal. Throughput small regression but acceptable. I created a perf ticket with traces and nvprof output: PERF-1423. Attached artifact links and cc @Sofia Morales @Lu Wang.
Raj Patel: Next steps: (1) add a regression test that simulates KV prefetch fragmentation on EFA topology, (2) refine kernelselect cost model to include per-op NCCL penalty for cross-node fabrics, (3) measure chunked-reduce vs consolidated reduce tradeoffs.
Mira Chen: Agreed. I'll add the test harness and upload baseline traces to PERF-1423. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
